title: Goldilocks & the Three Bears
strapline: Too big, too small, just right — a whole story made of comparing.
intent: This tale is early maths dressed as a story: three sizes of bowl, chair and bed to match, order and compare.
The repeating pattern — too hot, too cold, just right — gives children a rhythm to predict and join in with.
Retelling a story they know well lets children hold a beginning, middle and end and sequence what comes next.
Goldilocks doing the wrong thing opens gentle talk about choices, saying sorry and how the bears might feel.
The three-bears' cottage becomes a small world for porridge-making, tidying and putting everything right.
implementation: Set up the cottage with three of everything in three clear sizes — bowls, spoons, chairs, beds — plus a Goldilocks and three bears.
Tell the story with the props first, landing hard on 'too big, too small, just right', then hand the play over.
Sit alongside and wonder: 'Which bowl belongs to which bear? How can we tell?'
Weave in size and order language — biggest, middle, smallest, tallest — and invite children to line things up.
Model the feelings talk: 'The little bear is sad his chair is broken — what could Goldilocks say to him?'
Follow the play — some children will sort and match all morning, others will make porridge and lay the table.
key_questions: Which bowl belongs to Baby Bear — how do you know?
Can you put the beds in order from biggest to smallest?
What happened first, and what came next?
How does Baby Bear feel about his broken chair?
What could Goldilocks say to make it better?

impact.text: Children match and order objects by size and use words like big, middle and smallest.
Children retell the story in rough sequence and join in the repeated pattern.
Children talk about the characters' feelings and what would put things right.
Children play out the cottage scene — making porridge, laying the table, tidying up.
Children predict the next 'just right' and use talk to direct the play.

enhancements: A porridge station — real oats to scoop, three bowls, three spoons — for making breakfast for the bears.
A size-ordering challenge: mixed-up bears, bowls and beds to sort back into families.
Story puppets or masks so children can act it out and take the parts.
A 'sorry' card-making table for Goldilocks to apologise to Baby Bear.
A den or cottage children can climb into to be the bears coming home.

playing_exploring: Children sort, match and pretend, following the story wherever their interest takes it.
They test which thing belongs to which bear, arranging and rearranging.
active_learning: Children take on the porridge-making and table-laying and see the routine through.
They persist at ordering all three sizes until every bear has the right one.
creating_thinking: Children reason about size — how they know a bowl is Baby Bear's — and explain it.
They imagine what happens after the story ends and act it out.
